blocks.value: Until now, you've learned why stock prices move. But how do investors understand what has happened over time? The answer is a stock chart.

Imagine This: Every month your teacher records your marks in Maths. Looking at a single month's score tells very little, but seeing all your scores on a graph instantly shows whether you're improving or struggling. A stock chart does the same thing for share prices.
A stock chart is a visual representation of how a stock's price has changed over time. Instead of reading thousands of numbers, investors can quickly understand trends by looking at a chart.
If Reliance moved from ₹2,200 to ₹2,700 over six months, a chart makes that movement easy to understand.
Charts don't predict the future—they help us understand what has happened so we can make better decisions.

blocks.question: Why do investors use stock charts?
choices: To understand price movements over time.
